claims.text: Machine-learning-guided adjustment of non-equiatomic composition and annealing parameters can tune magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior in a disordered HEA.
Adjusting composition and annealing parameters tunes local chemical environments.
Changes in local chemical environments modify magnetic exchange interactions.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions can enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
The initial non-equiatomic HEA is a disordered multielement metallic mixture.
The initial alloy has inherent chemical inhomogeneity.
Machine learning can be used to select concentrations of key magnetic elements and annealing temperature and time.
The proposed processing produces enhanced local chemical inhomogeneity and modified atomic-scale environments.
Modified atomic-scale environments alter magnetic exchange pathways.
Optimization of non-equiatomic composition and thermal processing tailors the electronic structure and local magnetic interactions.
Tailoring the electronic structure and local magnetic interactions produces a controlled shift in magnetic ordering.
Moving the magnetic phase transition closer to the operating temperature improves the magnetocaloric response.
The optimization influences the magnitude of the magnetic entropy change.
Optimized samples will show a magnetic phase-transition shift toward the target operating regime relative to conventionally processed controls.
Optimized samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric effect, such as a larger magnetic entropy change, than samples made using standard processing.
The proposed relationship applies only while processing preserves the alloy's disordered high-entropy characteristics.
The proposed relationship may not extend to over-annealed or overly crystallized systems.
